rationale: The mass reads coherently across the four views as one compact object with a dominant carved/stepped gesture and a clear top-to-bottom hierarchy. It is not just filling a box: the sloped massing and the apparent central/top void create a recognizable open-space figure. The main weakness is that the public threshold is not very strongly articulated along the verified access edge; the building feels more sealed than invitational on the road side. Still, the form remains plausible for neighborhood living/commercial support, with a capacity-aware low-rise section and a defensible courtyard/void logic. It is not overly stair-like in a code-minimum sense because the stepping is read as one continuous landform, though it leans slightly toward a sculpted bar rather than an explicitly active street building.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-centered low-rise composition with connected wings and a legible terrace/ribbon circulation idea.
